title: The Dropping Rule
rule: When a word ends in a silent e and the ending starts with a vowel (ing, er, est, ed), drop the e: bake becomes baking. If the ending starts with a consonant (ly, ful, less, ness), keep the e: safe becomes safely.
trickText: Look at the ending. Does it start with a vowel? Drop the silent e. Does it start with a consonant? Keep the e.
say: Today's case: the dropping rule. When a word ends in a silent e and the ending starts with a vowel, we drop the e. Bake plus i n g makes baking. But if the ending starts with a consonant, we keep the e, like safely.

activities.instruction: Do you drop the silent e, or keep it?

categories.label: Drop the e
categories.why: The ending starts with a vowel, so drop the silent e.

categories.label: Keep the e

categories.label: Double the last letter
categories.why: One short vowel and one ending consonant before a vowel ending.

categories.label: Drop the e
categories.why: A silent e before a vowel ending.
